claims: C1 the role of a message specifies the source of that message
C2 roles determine the authority of instructions in the case of conflicts
C3 authority is determined according to the levels of authority and chain of command

concepts.name: message_role_definition
concepts.gloss: the role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies the source of the message and determines the authority of its instructions in conflicts

concepts.name: message_role
concepts.gloss: message M has role R, where R is one of system, developer, user, assistant, or tool

concepts.name: message_source
concepts.gloss: message M originates from source S, as specified by its role

concepts.name: instruction_authority
concepts.gloss: instruction I has authority level A, as determined by the role of the message that carries it

concepts.name: conflicting_instructions
concepts.gloss: instruction I1 and instruction I2 conflict with each other
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'the case of conflicts', so a relation identifying which instructions conflict is presupposed

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control

concepts.name: role_source
concepts.gloss: role R specifies that messages with that role originate from source S
concepts.inference: the clause says a role specifies the source of a message, so each role must be associated with a source

concepts.name: carries_instruction
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of the authority of instructions, so instructions must be carried by messages

concepts.name: role_authority
concepts.gloss: role R confers authority level A on the instructions it carries
concepts.inference: the clause says roles determine the authority of instructions, so each role must be associated with an authority level

ontology.gloss: R is a message role that specifies the source of a message and determines the authority of its instructions
message M's source S is specified by its role
instruction I's authority A is determined by the role of the message carrying it
ontology.body: message_role(M, R), carries_instruction(M, I), role_authority(R, A)
